items.title: Jensen Huang's 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership' letter doubles from 25 to 50 signatories in a single day — OpenAI and Google both flip and join over the weekend, along with AMD, Cisco, Cloudflare, GitHub, Block, Ollama, Palantir, ServiceNow, Replit, Cohere, Andreessen Horowitz, Palo Alto Networks and 12 others; Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI remain conspicuously absent as of Sunday afternoon July 26, with Anthropic now the only US frontier lab still off the list and its silence increasingly framed as the more revealing signal than the letter itself
items.summary: NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang on Thursday July 24, 2026 made his debut post on X — using it to share an open letter that NVIDIA signed alongside 24 other organizations, arguing that open-weight AI models are essential to safety, cybersecurity, innovation, and sovereignty, and warning Washington against restricting Chinese open-weight models. Huang's specific framing: 'AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.' The initial 25-org signatory list captured in this morning's am snapshot included NVIDIA, Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Dell Technologies, Mistral, Mozilla, Hugging Face, The Linux Foundation, Perplexity, Y Combinator, and 14 others — with the specific notable absentees flagged as Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind. In the roughly 36 hours since the letter first published, the signatory list has effectively doubled: Forbes reported Saturday July 25 (Sandy Carter, contributor) that the letter had already reached 50 signatories, and by Sunday afternoon July 26 the published list on the letter's Nvidia-hosted page includes AI21, AMD, American Innovators Network, AMP, Andreessen Horowitz, Arcee AI, Arena, Baseten, Black Forest Labs, Block, Box, Cisco, Cloudflare, Cohere, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, DoorDash, Emergence Capital, Fireworks AI, Genspark, GitHub, Google, Hugging Face, IBM, Inferact, Interconnects AI, The Linux Foundation, Mariana Minerals, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, Morph, Mozilla, Nebius, Nous Research, NVIDIA, Ollama, OpenAI, OpenClaw, Palantir, Palo Alto Networks, Periodic Labs, Perplexity, Prime Intellect, Reflection, Replit, ServiceNow, Telnyx, Trajectory, and Y Combinator. The two specific weekend flips that matter most: OpenAI and Google, both explicitly called out as absentees in Friday's initial announcement, added their names over Saturday and Sunday. The remaining conspicuous absentees as of Sunday afternoon July 26 are Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI. Multiple outlets (Forbes, Startup Fortune, Benzinga, Tom's Hardware) have consolidated around the specific framing that Anthropic's continued silence is now the more revealing signal than the letter itself — the interpretation runs from 'plain commercial interest, since Anthropic sells closed frontier access' to 'a substantive safety position that weights once released cannot be recalled,' with Anthropic's own CEO Dario Amodei previously calling open source 'a red herring' as the specific philosophical marker of the closed-weights safety position. The policy context has not changed: the letter still lands as the White House debates whether to restrict US access to Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 (2.8T open-weight frontier model, full weights on Modified MIT license arriving tonight at 8pm ET / 00:00 UTC July 27 — see today's am snapshot for the specific technical and hardware-requirement detail), and Huang's specific historical argument remains that Washington should not repeat the mistake of considering restrictions on open-source software in the early 1980s.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: this is a specific US-open-weights-policy signal that matters for two structural reasons and one practical hobbyist reason. First, the specific coalition read: 25 US technology organizations publicly signing a letter that argues open-weight AI models are essential to national security and sovereignty is the specific structural signal that the US open-vs-closed weights debate has reached the 'coalition-forms-around-position' stage rather than remaining a debate confined to research communities. The specific pattern to note is who did NOT sign: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind — the three US frontier labs whose business model most depends on closed-weights differentiation. That split maps cleanly onto the underlying commercial interest: closed-weights labs benefit from restrictions that raise the cost of open-weights competition (Kimi K3, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek), while cloud vendors and inference platforms benefit from open-weights ubiquity. The specific pattern-recognition to carry: US open-vs-closed-weights policy is now a specific commercial-alignment fight where you can predict which company signs which letter by looking at their revenue model, not by looking at their public rhetoric about AI safety. Second, the specific Kimi-K3-timing read: the July 27 Kimi K3 open-weights release (tonight at 8pm ET, under Modified MIT license) is the specific event that this letter is designed to shape the response to. If the White House restricts US access to Kimi K3 weights, US open-weights-inference vendors (Hugging Face, Together AI, Fireworks, Groq, Cerebras) lose the flagship model that most demonstrates their competitive value proposition. If the White House does not restrict, then a Chinese lab has just seeded US infrastructure with the largest open-weight frontier model to date. The specific practical timeline is 'watch what happens between Sunday July 27 and next Friday' — if there's a White House statement or executive action in that window, the letter's coalition just became the specific counter-lobby. Third, the specific practical hobbyist read: as a Python developer who might want to run frontier-quality models locally or on a rented GPU, the specific outcome of this policy debate directly determines whether Kimi K3 will be available for you to download and self-host next week. If the White House restricts, the practical channels for a US-based hobbyist to try Kimi K3 will narrow to the hosted Moonshot API and third-party VPN-based workarounds — which is a specific practical friction to be aware of. If the White House stays hands-off, Kimi K3 becomes the specific 'largest frontier model you can run on rented hardware' benchmark for the rest of 2026. Fourth, the specific Huang-joins-X context worth noting: Huang has historically avoided X, and the fact that his first-ever post was this letter — rather than an NVIDIA-product post or a personal message — is the specific tell that NVIDIA is treating US open-weights policy as a first-order strategic priority. NVIDIA's specific commercial interest is that open-weights inference on NVIDIA GPUs is a much larger revenue base than closed-weights training contracts with a small number of frontier labs, so 'the world needs both' is the specific framing that maximizes NVIDIA's GPU-sales surface area. Fifth, the specific afternoon read that firmed up over the weekend and reshapes the story: the letter doubled from 25 to 50 signatories in roughly 36 hours, and — critically — OpenAI and Google both flipped from initial absentees to signatories over Saturday and Sunday. That specific reversal changes the shape of the story from 'US cloud vendors and open-weights labs vs. US frontier labs' into 'US industry consensus except Anthropic, Amazon, and xAI.' The specific practical implication of OpenAI joining is that Sam Altman has publicly moved his lab into the 'don't restrict Chinese open weights' camp exactly as OpenAI itself has been re-committing to open-weights releases (the gpt-oss lineage). The specific practical implication of Google joining is that DeepMind — which does not currently ship frontier open weights — has publicly aligned with the coalition anyway, signaling that Google's commercial calculus prioritizes broad developer access on Google Cloud over closed-weights differentiation on Gemini. Sixth, the specific Anthropic-as-lone-holdout read that is now the story: with OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Meta, NVIDIA, IBM, Dell, and every major open-weights lab except Cohere-until-now aligned on one side, Anthropic's continued silence is the specific structural signal that matters more than the letter's rhetoric. Multiple outlets (Startup Fortune, Forbes, Benzinga) have consolidated around the framing that Anthropic is now the only US frontier lab whose commercial model actively requires closed-weights competitive advantage — a positioning consistent with Dario Amodei's 'open source is a red herring' framing, but a positioning that puts Anthropic on the same side of the US open-weights debate as, essentially, nobody else that matters commercially. The specific practical implication for Gabe: if you use Claude for any professional work, Anthropic's lonely-holdout position on open weights is now a specific business-risk read worth carrying — it's the specific bet that closed-weights differentiation on capability can outweigh the industry-wide commercial pressure to align with open-weights consensus. The specific pattern to watch through next week: whether Anthropic issues any public statement, whether Anthropic ends up on any updated letter, and whether the White House's Kimi K3 response singles out Anthropic's absence as a policy signal.

items.title: Chinese AI models sweep the OpenRouter top 10 as of the weekend of July 25-26 — 46.4% of routed tokens vs 35.7% for US models, only Anthropic's Claude at 13.3% survives among the top ten as OpenAI, Google, and Meta all drop off; the specific market-share signal that hardened over the past week and is now the specific number the Trump administration is citing in its Kimi K3 executive-order deliberations, hours before Kimi K3 open weights land tonight at 8pm ET
items.summary: OpenRouter usage data covered across multiple outlets over the weekend of July 25-26, 2026 shows a specific market-share threshold: Chinese-made AI models now account for 46.4% of all tokens routed through OpenRouter — the popular API-aggregation platform US developers use to plug into multiple AI models through a single API — while US-made models have fallen to 35.7%. The specific weekend-of-July-25-26 update on top of the July 7 CNBC figures: Chinese models now claim eight of the top ten most-used models on the platform, with only Anthropic's Claude family (Claude at 13.3% aggregate token share across the Claude family) remaining as a US-lab representative in the top ten. OpenAI and Google, previously top-3 fixtures on OpenRouter for most of 2024-2025, have both dropped out of the top ten entirely. The specific historical trajectory: Chinese models were at 4.5% weekly token share in the first half of 2025, then 11% averaged over the twelve months prior to mid-2026, then hit a weekly peak of 46% in mid-2026 (per CNBC's July 7 investigation), and are now — per BigGo Finance and Yahoo Finance coverage this weekend — sweeping the top-10 leaderboard entirely. The specific price-mechanism read is unchanged from the running story: DeepSeek V4 Flash costs $0.14 per million input tokens against OpenAI's GPT-5.5 at $5.00, and comparable open-weight Chinese models across DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, and Qwen sit in the $0.14-to-$0.60 range against US closed-weight flagships at $2.50-to-$12.00 per million input tokens — a specific 4x-to-100x price differential that maps directly to the token-volume shift. The Yahoo Finance angle (framed for enterprise CFOs): 'Chinese AI Models Now Capture Up to 46% of US Enterprise Token Usage' — the specific enterprise-adoption number that Washington is now citing in its executive-order deliberations. Timing context: the market-share data is hardening over the specific weekend that Kimi K3 open weights arrive tonight at 8pm ET (00:00 UTC July 27), which is the specific event that the Trump administration's reported Kimi-K3-triggered executive-order push is designed to address — and the specific data point that will get worse for US labs the moment K3 weights land and hosted-inference providers pick them up.
items.why_it_matters: For Gabe: three reads. First, the specific market-share read: as of this weekend, Chinese AI models are 46.4% of all API traffic on OpenRouter — the specific developer-tool US developers use to route requests across models — while US models are 35.7%. That's not a rounding error. That's the specific structural inversion where a year ago US models were ~70% of the same platform and Chinese models were ~5%. Every read from here has to start with 'Chinese open-weight AI is now the dominant volume story on developer API-aggregation platforms.' Second, the specific top-10 read: OpenAI and Google, both top-3 fixtures on OpenRouter for most of 2024-2025, have dropped OUT of the top ten most-used models entirely. The only US-lab representative in the top ten now is Anthropic's Claude family at 13.3% aggregate token share. That's a specific 'US closed-weights labs are being crowded out of developer-inference platforms by open-weight Chinese models' story that maps directly to the price-mechanism read: DeepSeek V4 Flash at $0.14/M input tokens vs OpenAI GPT-5.5 at $5.00/M is a 35x price gap, and for developers building applications where token cost is a real budget line rather than a rounding error, that gap is decisive. The specific practical implication for anyone using OpenRouter (or LangChain/LlamaIndex model routing) in a Python project: your default model choice for high-volume paths is probably no longer OpenAI or Google. Third, the specific policy-tie-in read that makes this a Sunday-July-26 story rather than a generic 'Chinese models are eating US market share' story: the specific 46.4% number is now what the Trump administration is citing in its Kimi K3 executive-order deliberations (per this weekend's Axios follow-up reporting via Yahoo and Cryptobriefing coverage). The specific timing: Kimi K3 open weights land TONIGHT at 8pm ET, which is the specific event that will accelerate this trend further — hosted-inference providers (Together AI, Fireworks, Groq, Cerebras) will pick up K3 weights within days, K3 becomes the flagship low-cost open-weight route on OpenRouter within weeks, and the 46.4% number likely climbs to 55-60% before Q4 2026. That's the specific concrete data point behind the Jensen Huang open-weights letter (also in this snapshot) and the specific Trump-executive-order-consideration policy fork. Fourth, the specific practical tie-in to Gabe's stack: if you use OpenRouter or any model-aggregation router for a Python project, the specific practical action is to look at your current default model routing — if you're defaulting to GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, or Gemini 3.6 Pro on any high-volume path, the specific cost-quality tradeoff has shifted enough over the past three weeks (Kimi K3 API pricing, DeepSeek V4 Flash pricing, GLM-5.2 pricing) that you should re-evaluate at least one path against a Chinese open-weight model this week. That's not a political choice — it's the specific cost read where a $0.14/M-input model that matches or beats GPT-5.5 on your specific task is the specific correct default for cost-sensitive high-volume paths.
